active_paradigms.idea: Bisection on KVPR threshold with exact subset-sum DP feasibility instead of FFD bin-packing
active_paradigms.description: Keep the bisection framework (feasibility of threshold T is monotone), but replace the FFD heuristic with an exact feasibility check. For a candidate T, each model i has virtual size v_i = w_i + T*s_i and bins have capacity 80*T; feasibility is a bin-packing decision problem. Since model counts and gpu counts are typically small, solve it exactly: enumerate feasible subsets of models per bin via recursive backtracking with memoization on remaining items and per-bin residual capacity, or a subset-sum DP over discretized virtual sizes. Alternatively, use a much stronger heuristic set: try FFD, best-fit-decreasing, and also a first-fit-increasing / size-sorted order, and a randomized-restart FFD with many random permutations (e.g., 200 restarts taking the best feasible packing). The key insight is that FFD alone often declares a T infeasible when it is actually feasible, so bisection converges to a T above the true optimum; exact or heavily randomized feasibility closes this gap.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The minimal feasible KVPR threshold found by bisection (directly reduces max KVPR, improving the evaluator score 1/avg_KVPR).
active_paradigms.cautions: Backtracking must be bounded (node/time limits) to avoid timeouts on larger instances; fall back to FFD if the exact check exceeds a time budget. Use epsilon tolerance 1e-9 in capacity checks. Random restarts should be seeded deterministically for reproducibility.

active_paradigms.idea: Large Neighborhood Search (LNS): iteratively destroy the worst-KVPR GPUs and optimally repack their models via bisection-restricted packing
active_paradigms.description: Start from the current bisection+FFD placement. In each iteration, identify the 1-2 GPUs with highest KVPR, remove all their models (plus optionally a few random models from other GPUs), and repack those models optimally among the affected GPUs using the virtual-size bisection packing restricted to those bins — a much smaller subproblem solved near-exactly (exhaustive permutation or exact backtracking since item count is tiny). Accept if the global max KVPR decreases; also allow occasional equal-value or simulated-annealing-style acceptance with a small temperature to escape local optima. Run until no improvement for several iterations or a time cap. This directly attacks the weakness of the current single-pass move/swap local search, which only moves one model at a time and gets stuck: LNS reoptimizes entire GPUs jointly.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduction of the global maximum KVPR below what pairwise move/swap local search can reach.
active_paradigms.cautions: Cap total iterations (e.g., 100) and per-repack time; always keep the best placement found, never return a worse one. Keep the existing feasible placement as fallback if anything fails. Deterministic seed for random perturbations.

active_paradigms.idea: Balance-aware initialization: minimize per-GPU ratio directly via sorted greedy on KVPR contribution and load-to-free matching, plus final equalization pass
active_paradigms.description: A fundamentally different constructive approach: compute for each model its KVPR-in-isolation rho_i = (w_i/s_i) * 1/(80/s_i - 1)... more simply, note a GPU's KVPR is (sum w)/(80 - sum s); target placements where every GPU has the same ratio of total w to total s. Sort models by w/s density and assign each next model to the GPU that minimizes the resulting KVPR (best-fit on ratio, tie-break by most free memory), which is a 'ratio-balancing' greedy distinct from virtual-size packing. Then run a final equalization pass: repeatedly move the model with the smallest w from the highest-KVPR GPU to the lowest-KVPR GPU whenever it strictly reduces the max. Finally, compare this placement's max KVPR against the bisection placement and return the better one — an ensemble-of-constructions strategy where the cheap ratio-greedy sometimes beats packing-based methods, especially when many models share similar sizes.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct minimization of per-GPU KVPR ratio balance at construction time, as an alternative/ensemble to the virtual-size bisection.
active_paradigms.cautions: Guard against zero free memory (skip placements that leave free <= 0); must place every model even if max KVPR worsens (fallback to any-memory-fit). Ensemble selection must compute true max KVPR identically to the evaluator (including empty GPUs excluded from max).
active_paradigms.approach_type: greedy ratio-balancing construction (ensemble with existing bisection)

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary search on target KVPR threshold with a bin-packing-style feasibility check on the combined weight 'w + T*size'
tried_paradigms.description: Key structural insight: a GPU holding subset S satisfies KVPR <= T iff sum(w_i) <= T*(80 - sum(s_i)), which rearranges to sum(w_i + T*s_i) <= 80*T. So for a candidate threshold T, each model gets a virtual size v_i = w_i + T*s_i, and feasibility becomes: pack all items with virtual sizes v_i into gpu_num bins of capacity 80*T using first-fit-decreasing (plus a fallback best-fit). This feasibility test is monotone in T, so run bisection on T (e.g., 40 iterations between 0 and a safe upper bound from the current greedy solution) to find the minimal feasible T. Then construct the actual placement from the packing at the best feasible T, and run a short local-search polish (moves/swaps) to shave the true max KVPR further, since FFD packing is only a heuristic for feasibility. Keep the current greedy as an upper-bound seed so the result is never worse than 25.8.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score (mean of per-case max KVPR) by directly minimizing the achievable KVPR threshold rather than improving incrementally
tried_paradigms.cautions: Handle the edge case where a single item's virtual size exceeds 80*T (infeasible at that T, raise threshold). Wrap FFD in a try for gpu_num small; ensure free memory stays strictly positive in the final placement (v_i < 80T guarantees s_i < 80 when w_i>0, but add an explicit check for zero-rate models). Bisection tolerance ~1e-9 relative.

tried_paradigms.idea: Multi-start randomized greedy construction with simulated-annealing local search over moves and pairwise swaps
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the single deterministic greedy with N (e.g., 30-60) restarts, each using a different randomized priority order (weighted shuffle biased toward req_rate/slo descending, seeded deterministically for reproducibility). For each construction, run an annealing local search: neighborhood = single-model moves between GPUs and pairwise swaps, with the objective being the global max KVPR (plus a small tie-breaking term like sum of squared KVPRs to smooth the landscape out of local minima on the max). Accept slightly worsening moves with probability exp(delta/temperature), geometric cooling. Keep the best solution across all restarts and return it. This attacks the weakness that the current greedy + hill-climber gets trapped: the max-KVPR objective is flat with respect to most moves, so annealing with the secondary smooth objective escapes plateaus.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score by escaping local optima of the max-KVPR landscape that trap the current hill-climber
tried_paradigms.cautions: Cap total runtime (e.g., a wall-clock budget of a few seconds per test case) since the evaluator has a timeout; use a fixed RNG seed so results are deterministic; always keep memory feasibility (free > 0 after placement); precompute w = req_rate/slo per model once per restart.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact branch-and-bound with a load-balancing lower bound for small instances, heuristic fallback for large ones
tried_paradigms.description: Test cases with few models (say <= 12) can be solved near-optimally: do a depth-first branch-and-bound that assigns models one at a time (ordered by w descending) to each GPU, pruning a branch if the partial max KVPR already meets or exceeds the best complete solution found so far, and pruning with a lower bound: total_load must be split across at most gpu_num active GPUs, and each GPU's denominator is at most 80 minus its smallest placed model size, giving LB = max over GPUs of a fractional relaxation (e.g., best possible KVPR if all remaining load went to the emptiest/highest-free GPU). Memoize dominant states. For larger instances, fall back to the current greedy followed by the stronger local search. Also add a preprocessing insight: zero-rate models (w=0) should each be placed alone or grouped together on dedicated GPUs since they add zero load but consume free memory — assign them last to empty GPUs or the GPU with zero-load models only, which the current algorithm mishandles.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via provably (near-)optimal placements on small cases and smarter handling of zero/low-rate models
tried_paradigms.cautions: Guard the exact search with a node-count limit (e.g., 200k nodes) to avoid timeouts; the pruning must compare max over only non-empty GPUs correctly; ensure fallback path is always available; handle gpu_num >= model count by checking the one-model-per-GPU upper bound first as an initial incumbent.
